html:
SMTO-CMP-0037 — The AI pointed to a step that never actually ran

GUID: d8669b97-1a12-4f97-ae10-8dc37b18fd1a
Slug: completion-unexecuted-evidence
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI tried to prove the task was done using a step that was only planned or was blocked, so it never ran. SMTO asked the AI to show work that actually happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Expand the task and find the step that didn't run. Look for labels such as Not run, Rejected or Needs approval. The label shows whether the step was blocked by a check, waiting for approval or denied.
  2. If the step is waiting for your approval, read what it will do and approve or deny it. If you denied it earlier, decide whether you still want it. A step that needs approval won't run until someone approves it.
  3. Send a message asking SMTO to run the step now, or to finish without it if you no longer want it. This gives the AI a clear go-ahead, so it reports real results instead of a plan.

What success looks like

  • The step shows Completed with real output, and the task finishes as Completed.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If a safety check blocked the step, don't turn that check off just to get the task finished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion was rejected because a cited result-index entry or durable receipt has executed=false, so it records only a proposal or rejection, not actual execution.

What this means

  • A cited result/index or durable receipt has executed false when completion requires evidence of actual execution. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • A cited result/index or durable receipt has executed false when completion requires evidence of actual execution.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare durable executed facts with the cached index and original admission receipt.

How to fix it

  • Compare the result index and the durable receipt for the cited operation, including its original authorization outcome. Execute the operation through its normal authorization path (or drop the claim) and cite the executed receipt; an unexecuted proposal can never establish completion.
  • Obtain authoritative execution evidence; an unexecuted proposal cannot establish completion.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Only actually executed eligible evidence supports the completion claim.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
